summary.name: SRE fundamentals: SLIs, SLAs and SLOs
summary.one_liner: A 2018 Google Cloud Blog article explaining the site reliability engineering (SRE) terms service-level indicator (SLI), service-level objective (SLO), and service-level agreement (SLA) and how to apply them.
use_cases: Defining availability targets for a service
Deciding whether a system needs more or less reliability
Writing SLAs with penalties for paying customers
Measuring SLO compliance with logs and monitoring
Setting up SLIs in a Google Cloud dashboard
summary.what_it_does: The article defines SLO, SLA and SLI as SRE planning tools. An SLO is a numeric availability target for a system, which should be set at the lowest reliability the service can afford. An SLA is a customer-facing promise, usually with a penalty such as a partial refund, and is normally looser than the internal SLO (for example 99.9% against an internal 99.95%). An SLI is the measured rate of successful probes or queries, used to check whether the system is meeting its SLO. It also notes that Google Cloud Stackdriver can combine custom SLIs with GCP service SLIs on one dashboard.
notable: Explains why the SLA target is usually looser than the internal SLO
Covers excluding invalid queries, such as out-of-quota responses, from SLA accounting
Written by Google Cloud product managers as a refresher from Google CRE posts
